label: prop:conic
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:conic}
  Let \(F(x_1,x_2) = a x_1^2 + b x_1x_2 + c x_2^2 + d x_1 + e x_2 + f\) with \(D = b^2 - 4 a c \neq 0\) be a smooth affine conic over \(\FF_q\) for \(q\) odd prime power. Then
  \[
    \left\lvert\ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}_F\right\rvert = \begin{cases}
      1       & \text{if } f' = 0     \text{ and } D \in \chi_q^{-1}(-1) \\
      q - 1   & \text{if } f' \neq 0  \text{ and } D \in \chi_q^{-1}(1)  \\
      q + 1   & \text{if } f' \neq 0  \text{ and } D \in \chi_q^{-1}(-1) \\
      2 q - 1 & \text{if } f' = 0     \text{ and } D \in \chi_q^{-1}(1),
    \end{cases}
  \]
  where \(f' = f + \frac{c d^2 - b d e + a e^2}{D}\).
head: environment

label: prop:count:lcd
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:count:lcd}
  Let \(n,k,q \in \ZZ\) with \(0 \leq k \leq n\) and \(q\) odd prime power. Denote by \(\mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{+1,0}\) (resp.~\(\mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{-1,0}\)) the set of all \([n,k]\)-linear LCD codes over \(\FF_q\) with a basis whose Gram matrix is \(\operatorname{diag}(1,\dots,1)\) (resp.~\(\operatorname{diag}(1,\dots,1,s)\) for some quadratic non-residue \(s \in \FF_q^\star\)), and as before by \(\mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^0\) the set of all \([n,k]\)-linear LCD codes over \(\FF_q\). Then \(\mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^0 = \mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{+1,0} \sqcup \mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{-1,0}\), and we have
  \[
    \left\lvert \mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{\pm1,0} \right\rvert =
    \begin{cases}
      \frac{1}{2} q^\frac{k \cdot (n-k) - 1}{2} A \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{\frac{n}{2}-1}{\frac{k-1}{2}}_{q^2} & \text{if \(k\) odd and \(n\) even}, \\
      \frac{1}{2} q^\frac{k \cdot (n-k)}{2} B_\pm \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{\frac{n-1}{2}}{\frac{k-1}{2}}_{q^2} & \text{if \(k\) odd and \(n\) odd}, \\
      \frac{1}{2} q^\frac{k \cdot (n-k)}{2} C_\pm \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{\frac{n-1}{2}}{\frac{k}{2}}_{q^2} & \text{if \(k\) even and \(n\) odd}, \\
      \frac{1}{2} q^\frac{k \cdot (n-k)}{2} D_\pm \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{\frac{n}{2}}{\frac{k}{2}}_{q^2} & \text{if \(k\) even and \(n\) even},
    \end{cases}
  \]
  where \(A = q^\frac{n}{2} - \chi_q(-1)^\frac{n}{2}\), \(B_\pm = q^\frac{n-k}{2} \pm \chi_q(-1)^\frac{n-k}{2}\), \(C_\pm = q^\frac{k}{2} \pm \chi_q(-1)^\frac{k}{2}\), \(D_\pm = \frac{\left( q^\frac{k}{2} \pm \chi_q(-1)^\frac{k}{2} \right) \cdot \left( q^\frac{n-k}{2} \pm \chi_q(-1)^\frac{n-k}{2} \right)}{\left( q^\frac{n}{2} + \chi_q(-1)^\frac{n}{2} \right)}\), hence
  \[
    \left\lvert \mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^0 \right\rvert =
    \begin{cases}
      q^\frac{k \cdot (n-k) - 1}{2} A \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{\frac{n}{2}-1}{\frac{k-1}{2}}_{q^2} & \text{if \(k\) odd and \(n\) even}, \\
      q^\frac{(k+1) \cdot (n-k)}{2} \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{\frac{n-1}{2}}{\frac{k-1}{2}}_{q^2} & \text{if \(k\) odd and \(n\) odd}, \\
      q^\frac{k \cdot (n-k+1)}{2} \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{\frac{n-1}{2}}{\frac{k}{2}}_{q^2} & \text{if \(k\) even and \(n\) odd}, \\
      q^\frac{k \cdot (n-k)}{2} \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{\frac{n}{2}}{\frac{k}{2}}_{q^2} & \text{if \(k\) even and \(n\) even}.
    \end{cases}
  \]

label: prop:count:hollow
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:count:hollow}
  Let \(n,k,h,q \in \ZZ\) with \(0 \leq h \leq k \leq n-h\) and \(q\) odd prime power. Denote by \(\mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{+1,h}\) (resp.~\(\mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{-1,h}\)) the set of all \([n,k]\)-linear codes over \(\FF_q\) with hull dimension \(h\) and a basis whose Gram matrix is \(\operatorname{diag}(1,\dots,1,0,\dots,0)\) (resp.~\(\operatorname{diag}(1,\dots,1,s,0,\dots,0)\) for some quadratic non-residue \(s \in \FF_q^\star\)), the number of \(0\)s being \(h\), and as before by \(\mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{h}\) the set of all \([n,k]\)-linear codes over \(\FF_q\) with hull dimension \(h\). Denote also \(t = k-h\). Then \(\mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{h} = \mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{+1,h} \sqcup \mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{-1,h}\) (where \(\mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{-1,k}\) is empty when \(h=k\)), and we have
  \[
    \left\lvert \mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{\pm1,h} \right\rvert =
    \begin{cases}
      C_1 \left\lvert \mathcal{X}_{n,t,q}^{\pm1,0} \right\rvert & \text{if \(n-t\) odd}, \\
      C_2 A_{\pm} \left\lvert \mathcal{X}_{n,t,q}^{\pm1,0} \right\rvert & \text{if \(n-t\) even},
    \end{cases}
  \]
  where \(A_\pm = \frac{q^{\frac{n-t}{2}-h} \pm \chi_q(-1)^\frac{n-t}{2}}{q^\frac{n-t}{2} \pm \chi_q(-1)^\frac{n-t}{2}}\) and \(C_i = \prod_{i=1}^{h} \frac{q^{n-t-2i+\ell} - 1}{q^{t} \cdot (q^i - 1)}\) for \(\ell \in \set{1,2}\), hence using \cref{prop:count:lcd} we have
  \[
    \left\lvert \mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{h} \right\rvert =
    \begin{cases}
      C_1 q^\frac{t \cdot (n-t) - 1}{2} B_- \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{\frac{n}{2}-1}{\frac{t-1}{2}}_{q^2} & \text{if \(t\) odd and \(n\) even}, \\
      C_2 q^{\frac{(t+1) \cdot (n-t)}{2} - h} \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{\frac{n-1}{2}}{\frac{t-1}{2}}_{q^2} & \text{if \(t\) odd and \(n\) odd}, \\
      C_1 q^\frac{t \cdot (n-t+1)}{2} \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{\frac{n-1}{2}}{\frac{t}{2}}_{q^2} & \text{if \(t\) even and \(n\) odd}, \\
      C_2 q^\frac{t \cdot (n-t)}{2} B_+ \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{\frac{n}{2}}{\frac{t}{2}}_{q^2} & \text{if \(t\) even and \(n\) even},
    \end{cases}
  \]
  where \(B_- = q^\frac{n}{2} - \chi_q(-1)^\frac{n}{2}\) and \(B_+ = \frac{q^{\frac{n}{2} - h} + \chi_q(-1)^\frac{n}{2}}{q^\frac{n}{2} + \chi_q(-1)^\frac{n}{2}}\).

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:so-variety}
  Let \(n,k,q \in \ZZ\) with \(0 < k \leq n\) and \(q\) prime power. Given a generator matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\) for an \([n,k]\)-linear code \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) over \(\FF_q\), a vector \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace = \ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace^\mathtt{T} \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace\) is self-orthogonal in \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) if and only if \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace\) is a root of the polynomial \(f_\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace) = \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace^\mathtt{T} \ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace \ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace^\mathtt{T} \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \in \FF_q[X_1,\dots,X_k]\) where \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace = [X_1,\dots,X_k]^\mathtt{T}\) is a vector of \(k\) variables over \(\FF_q\).

title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:code:variety}

For any generator matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\) for \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) we have \(\ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}_\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}} = \ensuremath{\left\{ \ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace^\mathtt{T} \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \; \middle\vert \; \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}_{f_\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace} \right\}}\).

label: lem:code:variety:nsols
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:code:variety:nsols}
  For every \([n,k]\)-linear code \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) over \(\FF_q\) we have \(\left\lvert \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}_\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}} \right\rvert \geq q^{k-2}\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace \in \FF_q^{k \times n}\) generate \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) and assume notation of \cref{prop:so-variety}. The \(k\)-variate polynomial \(f_\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\) of degree \(2\) over \(\FF_q\) is homogeneous, hence it has a root \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{0}}\xspace^k \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}_{f_\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace}\). If \(k > 2\), by Warning's Second Theorem~\cite[Satz~3]{HAM:Warning35} then \(\left\lvert \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}_{f_\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace} \right\rvert \geq q^{k-2}\) and hence by \cref{def:code:variety} also \(\left\lvert \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}_\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}} \right\rvert \geq q^{k-2}\). For \(k \leq 2\) it follows from \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{0}}\xspace^k \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}_\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) that \(\left\lvert \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}_\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}} \right\rvert \geq 1 \geq q^{k-2}\).

label: lem:hollow:plane
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:hollow:plane}
  A linear code over \(\FF_q\) for odd prime power \(q\) contains a regular plane if and only if it has hull co-dimension at least \(2\), and further contains a hyperbolic plane if and only if it has hull co-dimension at least \(3\) or hull co-dimension \(2\) and square class \(\chi_q(-1)\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Direct corollary of~\cite[Sec.~III.6]{Artin1957}. Any linear code with hull co-dimension at least \(3\) has an LCD component \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\) such that \(V_\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\) is regular. Then \(V_\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\) is isometric to an orthogonal sum of subspaces with at least one hyperbolic plane, which corresponds to a basis change of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\) that has the first two rows spanning a hyperbolic plane. When hull co-dimension is \(2\), we have that \(V_\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\) is either isometric to a hyperbolic plane, when \(\chi_\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace = \chi_q(-1)\), or to an anisotropic space, which corresponds to a non-hyperbolic regular plane. When hull co-dimension is \(1\) there are no regular planes, only one regular line for each hull vector.

label: prop:plane:hyper
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:plane:hyper}
  A regular plane over \(\FF_q\) for odd \(q\) contains a non-zero self-orthogonal vector if and only if it is hyperbolic.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\) span the plane. By~\cite[Sec.~III.6]{Artin1957}, there are exactly two possibilities for \(V_\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\) up to isometry, these are either the hyperbolic plane when \(\chi_\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace = \chi_q(-1)\), or the anisotropic representative. Since anisotropic spaces contain no non-zero isotropic vectors and isotropic vectors in \(V_\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\) are in bijective correspondence with self-orthogonal vectors in \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace)\) through \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \mapsto \ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace^\mathtt{T} \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace\), the conclusion follows.

body_md:
\label{def:algo:samplelcd}
  Let \(n,k,q,\chi \in \ZZ\) with \(0 \leq k \leq \frac{n}{2}\), \(\chi \in \set{\pm 1}\), and \(q\) odd prime power. Consider the algorithm in \cref{fig:algo:samplelcd} that on input \(n, k, q, \chi\) outputs a code generator matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\) with \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace) \in \mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{\chi,0}\) or aborts with \(\bot\). If \(k = 0\), the algorithm always outputs the zero code \(\set{\ensuremath{\mathbf{0}}\xspace^n}\).

name: Algorithm \(\SampleLCD\

label: lem:algo:samplelcd
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:algo:samplelcd}
  Assume the notation of \cref{def:algo:samplelcd}. The algorithm \(\ensuremath{\mathsf{SampleLCD}}\xspace\) runs in time \(\bigO{k \cdot (n^\omega + \log^2(q))}\), succeeds with probability overwhelming in \(k\), and its output distribution conditioned on not aborting is \(\dist_{n,k,q}^{\chi,0}\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The algorithm is in \cref{fig:algo:samplelcd} and is clearly correct if it succeeds with a matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\), as we are simply rejecting generator matrices with \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace) \notin \mathcal{X}_{n,k,q}^{\chi,h}\). The running time is immediate, since residue testing takes \(\log^2(q)\) by~\cite{Cohen1993}, so we focus on the success probability. The probability that a uniformly random matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace \sample \FF_q^{k \times n}\) is full-rank is \(p_\mathsf{FR} = \prod_{i=0}^{k-1} (1 - q^{i-n}) \geq 1 - \frac{k}{q^k}\), bound by the Weierstrass product inequality. Next, the probability that a uniformly random full-rank matrix generates an LCD code is at least \(\gamma_q\) by \cref{cor:prob-hull}. The probability that a uniformly random \(0\)-hollow matrix generates a code with square class \(\chi\) is by~\cite[Thm.~1]{localinv} at least \(\frac{1}{2} - q^{-\frac{k}{2}}\). The algorithm fails if in every one of the \(k\) repetitions at least one of these events does not happen. Using that \(\gamma_q \geq \frac{1}{2}\) by \cref{lem:prob-hull} for \(\bullet\), this probability is at most
  \begin{align*}
    \left(1 - \left(1 - k q^{-k}\right) \cdot \gamma_q \cdot \left(\frac{1}{2} - q^{-\frac{k}{2}}\right)\right)^k 
    &\overset{\bullet}{\leq} \left( 1 - \frac{1}{4} + \frac{k}{4} q^{-k} + \frac{1}{2} q^{-\frac{k}{2}} - \frac{k}{2} q^{-\frac{3k}{2}} \right)^k \\
    &\leq \left( \frac{3}{4} + \negl[k] \right)^k
    \leq \negl[k]. \qedhere
  \end{align*}

label: rem:algo:samplelcd
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:algo:samplelcd}
  An algorithm that samples uniformly random LCD codes without considering the square class can be obtained by removing the line that checks the square class. Alternatively we can instead sample \(\chi \sample \set{\pm 1}\) instead of taking it as input and obtain an algorithm whose output distribution is negligibly close in \(k\) to the uniform distribution on LCD codes.

label: def:algo:findplane
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:algo:findplane}
  Let \(n,k,h,q \in \ZZ\) with \(0 \leq h \leq k \leq n - h\), \(q\) odd prime power, and additionally \(h \leq k - 2\). Consider the algorithm \(\ensuremath{\mathsf{FindPlane}}\xspace\) in \cref{fig:algo:findplane} that on input an \(h\)-hollow matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace \in \FF_q^{k \times n}\) and indices \(i^* \neq j^*\) in \(\llbracket 1, k \rrbracket\), outputs a matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace \in \FF_q^{k \times n}\) such that \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace) = \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace)\), and \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace[i^*]\) and \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace[j^*]\) span a regular plane.
head: environment
name: Algorithm \(\FindPlane\

label: lem:algo:findplane
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:algo:findplane}
  The algorithm \(\ensuremath{\mathsf{FindPlane}}\xspace\) runs in time \(\bigO{n^\omega}\) and always succeeds.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Without loss of generality, suppose in this proof \(i^* = 1\) and \(j^* = 2\). Suppose for all rows \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace^\mathtt{T}\) of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\) we have \(\ensuremath{\left\langle \ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace \right\rangle} = 0\). Then there must exist two rows \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace^\mathtt{T}, \ensuremath{\mathbf{w}}\xspace^\mathtt{T}\) of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\) such that \(\ensuremath{\left\langle \ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathbf{w}}\xspace \right\rangle} \neq 0\), otherwise \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\) spans a self-orthogonal code. Thus \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace\) and \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{w}}\xspace\) span a regular plane, so our algorithm simply permutes the rows of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\) into \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace\) such that \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace\) starts with \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace\) and \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{w}}\xspace\), and clearly \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace) = \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace)\).

  Otherwise let \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace^\mathtt{T}\) be the first row of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\) with \(\ensuremath{\left\langle \ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace \right\rangle} \neq 0\). Compute a basis for the orthogonal complement of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace\) in \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace)\), that is, a generator matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace' \in \FF_q^{(k-1) \times n}\) for \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}} \cap \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace^\mathtt{T})^\mathtt{T}\) using the usual projections. Again, if for all rows \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{w}}\xspace^\mathtt{T}\) of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace'\) we have \(\ensuremath{\left\langle \ensuremath{\mathbf{w}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathbf{w}}\xspace \right\rangle} = 0\) then find any two rows of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace'\) that are not orthogonal, since it spans a code of hull co-dimension at least \(1\), and return \([\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace' \; \Vert \; \ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace^\mathtt{T}]\) permuted such that the two non-orthogonal rows of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace'\) are first. Otherwise let \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{w}}\xspace^\mathtt{T}\) be the first row that is not self-orthogonal in \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace'\). Then \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace\) and \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{w}}\xspace\) span a regular plane, hence return \([\ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace^\mathtt{T} \; \Vert \; \ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace']\) permuted such that \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace'\) starts with \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{w}}\xspace^\mathtt{T}\).

  The first condition can be checked with linear algebra by computing the Gram matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{G}}\xspace = \ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace^\mathtt{T}\) and checking whether it has all \(0\)s on the diagonal, and if so, finding \((i,j)\) such that \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{G}}\xspace_{i,j} \neq 0\) and permuting accordingly. Since we already have all the inner products from computing the Gram matrix, orthogonalisation costs \(k-1\) vector additions in \(\FF_q^n\).

Consider the algorithm \(\ensuremath{\mathsf{FindPlaneH}}\xspace\) in \cref{fig:algo:findplane:hyper} that on input an \(h\)-hollow matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace \in \FF_q^{k \times n}\) and indices \(i^* \neq j^*\) in \(\llbracket 1, k \rrbracket\), outputs a matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace \in \FF_q^{k \times n}\) such that \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace) = \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace)\), and \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace[i^*]\) and \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace[j^*]\) span a hyperbolic plane, or aborts with \(\bot\).

label: lem:algo:findplane:hyper
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:algo:findplane:hyper}
  The algorithm \(\ensuremath{\mathsf{FindPlaneH}}\xspace\) runs in time \(\bigO{n^\omega + \log^2(q)}\) and always succeeds, except when the input matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\) has hull co-dimension \(2\) and \(\chi_\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace \neq \chi_q(-1)\), in which case it always aborts.

title: Proof
body_md: The algorithm first finds any LCD component \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\) of the input \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\), runs \(\ensuremath{\mathsf{FindPlane}}\xspace\) and checks whether the obtained regular plane is already hyperbolic. Otherwise, we use the obtained regular plane to find any self-orthogonal vector in the span of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\) that is not already in the hull, for which it suffices to sample non-zero coefficients \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{c}}\xspace[1],\dots,\ensuremath{\mathbf{c}}\xspace[t-2]\) and pick any solution of the obtained affine conic, which exists by \cref{prop:conic}. Once we have a self-orthogonal vector \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace = \ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace^\mathtt{T} \ensuremath{\mathbf{c}}\xspace\) outside of the hull, constructing a hyperbolic plane is simple: pick any coefficient vector \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace\) such that \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace^\mathtt{T} \ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace^\mathtt{T} \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace = 1\) using linear algebra, orthogonally project it using \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{z}}\xspace = \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace - \frac{\ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace^\mathtt{T} \ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace^\mathtt{T} \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace}{2} \ensuremath{\mathbf{c}}\xspace\) and compute \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{w}}\xspace = \ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace^\mathtt{T} \ensuremath{\mathbf{z}}\xspace\). It is immediate that both \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace\) and \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{w}}\xspace\) are self-orthogonal, we have \(\ensuremath{\left\langle \ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathbf{w}}\xspace \right\rangle} = 1\), and so \([\ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace \mid \ensuremath{\mathbf{w}}\xspace]^\mathtt{T}\) generates a hyperbolic plane. Then simply compute a basis change of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\) such that it starts with \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{v}}\xspace\) and \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{w}}\xspace\), append the missing hull rows and permute the basis appropriately.

label: def:algo:sso
title: Definition
body_md:

label: def:torthogonality:vectors
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:torthogonality:vectors}
  Vectors \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace \in \FF_q^n\) are \emph{\(\phi_i\)-orthogonal} if \(\ensuremath{\left\langle \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace \right\rangle}_{\phi_i} = 0\), sometimes denoted as \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \perp_{\phi_i} \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace\). Two vectors that are \(\phi_i\)-orthogonal for every \(i \in \ZZ_d\) will be called \emph{totally orthogonal}. A vector is \emph{\(\phi_i\)-self-orthogonal} if it is \(\phi_i\)-orthogonal to itself. We call a vector \emph{totally self-orthogonal}, if it is \(\phi_i\)-self-orthogonal for every \(i \in \ZZ_d\).

name: Galois and total orthogonality of vectors

label: prop:torthogonality:bases
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:torthogonality:bases}
  Let \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace_1,\dots,\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace_t,\ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace_1,\dots,\ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace_s \in \FF_q^n\), and \(r \in \ZZ_d\) for \(q = p^d\). Then we have that for every \(i = 1,\dots,t\) and \(j = 1,\dots,s\) it holds \(\ensuremath{\left\langle \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace_i, \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace_j \right\rangle}_{\phi_r} = 0\) if and only if for every \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \in \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\set{\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace_i}_{i=1}^t)\) and every \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace \in \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\set{\ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace_j}_{j=1}^s)\) it holds \(\ensuremath{\left\langle \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace \right\rangle}_{\phi_r} = 0\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The if direction is clear, let us show the only if direction. It is clear from \(\FF_q\)-linearity in the first argument of \(\ensuremath{\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle}_{\phi_r}\) that if \(\ensuremath{\left\langle \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace_i, \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace \right\rangle}_{\phi_r} = 0\) for \(i=1,\dots,t\), then also \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\set{\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace_i}_{i=1}^t) \perp_{\phi_r} \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace_j\) for every \(j = 1,\dots,s\). For the second argument, where we only have \(\FF_p\)-linearity in general, observe that if \(\ensuremath{\left\langle \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace_i \right\rangle}_{\phi_r} = 0\) for \(i=1,\dots,k\) then
  \[
    \ensuremath{\left\langle \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace, \sum_{i=1}^{k} \alpha_i \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace_i \right\rangle}_{\phi_r}
    = \sum_{i=1}^{k} \phi_r(\alpha_i) \ensuremath{\left\langle \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace_i \right\rangle}_{\phi_r}
    = 0.
  \]
  Thus \(\phi_r\)-orthogonality of bases translates to \(\phi_r\)-orthogonality of their spans.

label: def:galois:hull
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:galois:hull}
  For a linear code \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}} \leq \FF_q^n\) and \(i \in \ZZ_d\) we define its \(i\)-th Galois dual as
  \[
    \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}^{\perp,\phi_i} = \ensuremath{\left\{ \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace \in \FF_q^n \; \middle\vert \; \forall \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \in \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}} \colon \ensuremath{\left\langle \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace \right\rangle}_{\phi_i} = 0 \right\}},
  \]
  and its \(i\)-th Galois hull as
  \[
    \operatorname{hull}_{\phi_i}(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}) = \ensuremath{\left\{ \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace \in \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}} \; \middle\vert \; \forall \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \in \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}} \colon \ensuremath{\left\langle \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace \right\rangle}_{\phi_i} = 0 \right\}} = \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}} \cap \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}^{\perp,\phi_i}.
  \]
  We give explicit algorithms to compute them in \cref{fig:galois:hull}.
head: environment
name: Galois dual and hull

label: def:totalort
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:totalort}
  Two linear codes \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}_1, \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}_2 \leq \FF_q^n\) are \(\phi_i\)-orthogonal if \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}_1 \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}_2^{\perp,\phi_i}\), or equivalently if \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}_2 \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}_1^{\perp,\phi_{d-i}}\). A linear code \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) is \(\phi_i\)-self-orthogonal if \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}} \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}^{\perp,\phi_i}\), and further totally self-orthogonal if this holds for every \(i \in \ZZ_d\).

name: Galois and total orthogonality of codes

label: rem:totalort
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:totalort}
  Note that \cref{def:totalort} of total (self-)orthogonality can be seen as a slight generalisation of~\cite[Def.~1.2.1]{NebeRainsSloane2006}, if we considered codes more broadly over rings. In~\cite[Def.~1.2.1]{NebeRainsSloane2006} codes over rings are endowed with a set of bilinear forms \(M\), and orthogonality is considered with respect to all forms in \(M\), much like our total orthogonality. The difference is that our forms \(\ensuremath{\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle}_{\phi_i}\) are generally not bilinear but \(\phi_i\)-sesquilinear.

label: def:totalhull
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:totalhull}

  \[
    \operatorname{hull}^\star(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}) = \bigcap_{i \in \ZZ_d} \operatorname{hull}_{\phi_i}(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}).

label: def:coefcode
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:coefcode}
  Let \(q = p^d\) for \(p\) prime and \(d \in \NN\), and fix \(f \in \FF_p[X]\) irreducible of degree \(d\) and \(z \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}_f\). For \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \in \FF_q^n\) define its \emph{coefficient code} as
  \[
    \Pi^{(f,z)}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace) = \operatorname{Span}_{\FF_p}\left(\ensuremath{\left\{ \pi_i^{(f,z)}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace) \; \middle\vert \; i \in \ZZ_d \right\}}\right).
  \]
  It is defined over \(\FF_p\), has length \(n\) and dimension at most \(d\).
head: environment
name: Coefficient code

label: def:moorecode
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:moorecode}
  Let \(q = p^d\) and \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \in \FF_q^n\). The \emph{Moore code} of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace\) is defined as
  \[
    \Phi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace) = \operatorname{Span}_{\FF_q}\left( \ensuremath{\left\{ \phi_i(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace) \; \middle\vert \; i \in \ZZ_d \right\}} \right).
  \]
  It is defined over \(\FF_q\), has length \(n\) and dimension at most \(d\).
head: environment
name: Moore code

title: Proposition
body_md: The following are equivalent: (i) the code \(\Phi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace)\) has dimension \(d\) over \(\FF_q\), (ii) the code \(\Pi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace)\) has dimension \(d\) over \(\FF_p\), and (iii) the entries of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace\) span \(\FF_q\) as a \(\FF_p\)-vector space.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The code \(\Phi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace)\) is generated by the matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{M}}\xspace_d(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace)^\mathtt{T}\) where \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace\) is viewed as a list of \(n\) elements in \(\FF_q\). By \cref{def:moore}, the determinant of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{M}}\xspace_d(a_1,\dots,a_d)\) is non-zero if and only if the elements \(a_1,\dots,a_d \in \FF_q\) are \(\FF_p\)-linearly independent, that is they form a basis for the \(\FF_p\)-vector space \(\FF_q \cong \FF_p^d\). This immediately implies that if \(n \geq d\) and \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \in \FF_q^n\) contains at least \(d\) \(\FF_p\)-linearly independent entries, which necessarily span \(\FF_q\) as an \(\FF_p\)-vector space, then \(\Phi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace)\) is full-rank and thus an \([n,d]\)-linear code over \(\FF_q\). The entries of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace\) span \(\FF_p^d\) precisely when the coefficient projection matrix \(\pi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace)\) spanning \(\Pi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace)\) has full rank \(d\). When \(n < d\) all statements are false, completing the proof.

label: prop:orthogonal
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write vectors \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace \in \FF_q^n\) as
  \[
    \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace = \left[\sum_{i=0}^{d-1} a_i^{(t)} z^i \right]_{t=1}^n
    \qquad
    \text{and}
    \qquad
    \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace = \left[\sum_{j=0}^{d-1} b_j^{(t)} z^j \right]_{t=1}^n,
  \]
  and compute
  \begin{align*}
    \ensuremath{\left\langle \ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace \right\rangle}_{\phi_r}
    &= \sum_{t=1}^{n} \left( \sum_{i=0}^{d-1} a_i^{(t)} z^i \right) \cdot \left( \sum_{j=0}^{d-1} b_j^{(t)} \phi_r(z^j) \right) 
    = \sum_{t=1}^{n} \sum_{i=0}^{d-1} \sum_{j=0}^{d-1} a_i^{(t)} b_j^{(t)} z^{i + j p^r} \\
    &= \sum_{i=0}^{d-1} \sum_{j=0}^{d-1} z^{i + j p^r} \left( \sum_{t=1}^{n} a_i^{(t)} b_j^{(t)} \right) 
    = \sum_{i=0}^{d-1} \sum_{j=0}^{d-1} z^{i + j p^r} \ensuremath{\left\langle \pi_i(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace), \pi_j(\ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace) \right\rangle}. \qedhere
  \end{align*}

label: lem:orthogonal
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:orthogonal}
  A sufficient condition that the vectors \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace\) and \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace\) are totally orthogonal is that \(\Pi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace)\) and \(\Pi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace)\) are orthogonal codes over \(\FF_p\) (that is one is in the dual of the other). In particular, if \(\Pi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace)\) is a self-orthogonal code over \(\FF_p\), then \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \in \FF_q^n\) is totally self-orthogonal.

label: thm:orthogonal
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:orthogonal}
  Two vectors \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace \in \FF_q^n\) are totally orthogonal if and only if \(\Pi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace)\) and \(\Pi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace)\) are orthogonal codes over \(\FF_p\). In particular, \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \in \FF_q\) is totally self-orthogonal if and only if \(\Pi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace)\) is a self-orthogonal code over \(\FF_p\).

title: Proof

label: rem:orthogonal
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:orthogonal}
  What may be surprising about \cref{thm:orthogonal} is that the crude method of setting every coefficient of the sum in \cref{prop:orthogonal} to \(0\) is the best we can do. In particular, this method \emph{ignores the multiplication structure} of \(\FF_q\), described by how the generator wraps around, and only treats \(\FF_q \cong \FF_p^d\) as an \(\FF_p\)-vector space.

title: Lemma
body_md:
Let \(q = p^d\) be any prime power. The following are equivalent: (i) the vectors \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace \in \FF_q^n\) are totally orthogonal, (ii) the codes \(\Phi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace), \Phi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace) \leq \FF_q^n\) are totally orthogonal, and (iii) the codes \(\Phi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace), \Phi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{y}}\xspace) \leq \FF_q^n\) are Euclidean orthogonal.
  In particular, \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \in \FF_q^n\) is totally self-orthogonal if and only if \(\Phi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace) \leq \FF_q^n\) is totally self-orthogonal, equivalently Euclidean self-orthogonal.

label: def:algo:sampletotal
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:algo:sampletotal}
  Let \(n,k,h,p,q,\chi \in \ZZ\) with \(0 \leq h \leq k \leq \frac{n}{2 d}\), \(\chi \in \set{\pm 1}\) (where \(\chi = 1\) when \(h=k\)), \(p\) odd prime and \(q = p^d\) for \(d \in \NN\). Consider the algorithm in \cref{fig:algo:sampletotal} that on input \(n,k,h,p,d,\chi\) outputs a generator matrix for a totally \(h\)-hollow \([n,k]\)-linear code over \(\FF_q\) with Euclidean square class \(\chi\) or aborts with \(\bot\).
head: environment
name: Algorithm \(\SampleTotal\

label: thm:algo:sampletotal
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:algo:sampletotal}
  Assume the notation of \cref{def:algo:sampletotal}. The algorithm \(\ensuremath{\mathsf{SampleTotal}}\xspace\) runs in time \(\poly[n,k,q]\), it succeeds with probability \(1 - \negl[k]\) unless \(d k = \frac{n}{2}\), \(h=k\) and \(\chi_p(-1)^{d k} \neq 1\) in which case it always aborts, and samples totally \(h\)-hollow \([n,k]\)-linear codes over \(\FF_q\) with Euclidean square class \(\chi\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The algorithm mimics \(\ensuremath{\mathsf{SampleCode}}\xspace\) but projects to \(\FF_p^n\) to sample total hull vectors. Indeed, we first sample a uniformly random (Euclidean) LCD code of dimension \(k-h\) and square class \(\chi\) over \(\FF_q\) identically to \(\ensuremath{\mathsf{SampleCode}}\xspace\). We then project \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\) to a \(d \cdot (k-h) \times n\) matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T'}}\xspace\) over \(\FF_p\) of rank \(t \leq d \cdot (k-h)\). We continue running the code of \(\ensuremath{\mathsf{SampleCode}}\xspace\) but over \(\FF_p\) and with a fixed \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace_{(0)} \coloneqq \ensuremath{\mathbf{T'}}\xspace\) (though \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace_{(0)}\) may have a hull over \(\FF_p\)). This produces \(d h\) hull vectors over \(\FF_p\), which we then lift \(d\) at a time using \(\pi^{-1}\) to \(\FF_q^n\) to obtain \(h\) total hull vectors.
  Denote by \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace_i\) for \(i=1,\dots,h\) disjoint groups of \(d\) consecutive rows of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{H}}\xspace\) and the same for \(i=h+1,\dots,k\) and \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace_{(0)}\). Denote also \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}_i = \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace_i)\). By construction, the codes \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}_i\) are jointly linearly independent and we have \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}_i \perp \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}_j\) for \(i=1,\dots,h\) and \(j=1,\dots,k\), hence immediately from \cref{thm:orthogonal} and \cref{prop:torthogonality:bases} the algorithm \(\ensuremath{\mathsf{SampleTotal}}\xspace\) is correct. Note that it is possible that the projected matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace_{(0)}\) has rank smaller than \(d \cdot (k-h)\), or that it has a hull. However, the algorithm is still correct, since the only vectors that get lifted back to \(\FF_q^n\) are the generated hull vectors which are by \cref{thm:orthogonal} totally orthogonal to \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\) and each other, and linearly independent of \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\). Observe also that the output \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\) generates precisely a totally \(h\)-hollow code, not some larger total hull dimension, since \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\) spans an LCD code and so the Euclidean hull dimension cannot be larger than \(h\). It is possible for an individual Galois hull to have dimension larger than \(h\). Running time and success probability follow from \cref{thm:algo:samplecode}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: We make no claims in \cref{thm:algo:sampletotal} about the output distribution of \(\ensuremath{\mathsf{SampleTotal}}\xspace\) (conditioned on not aborting), except that its support is a subset of all totally \(h\)-hollow \([n,k]\)-linear codes over \(\FF_q\) with Euclidean square class \(\chi\), though we suspect it is close to the uniform distribution on the whole set.

label: cor:attack
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:attack}
  Let \(p\) odd prime and \(n,k,h,d \in \NN\) with \(k \leq \frac{n}{2 d}\) and \(h \leq k\). Under the assumptions of the attack from~\cite{ITIT:BatMorSan26}, a necessary condition for codes sampled using \(\ensuremath{\mathsf{SampleTotal}}\xspace\) from \cref{def:algo:sampletotal} forming hard (search or distinguish) \(\operatorname{PCE}\) instances is that \(2d \cdot (4d - 1) < n\), that is roughly \(d < \sqrt{\frac{n}{8}}\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Without loss of generality, we may assume \(h=k\), since the algorithm from~\cite{ITIT:BatMorSan26} depends on the rate of the hull. Because the rate of \(\ensuremath{\mathsf{SampleCode}}\xspace\) is bounded by \(\frac{1}{2}\) from above, we must have \(d k \leq \frac{n}{2}\). On the other hand, to thwart the algorithm from~\cite{ITIT:BatMorSan26}, it is required that \(\binom{k+1}{2} > n\) for the coefficient lifted code over \(\FF_q\). Combining these, we obtain that \(4 d k < k \cdot (k+1)\), which implies \(d < \frac{k + 1}{4}\). Multiplying by \(4d\) and rearranging the inequality we get that
  \[
    (2 d)^2 - d < d k \leq \frac{n}{2}
    \qquad
    \text{hence}
    \qquad
    2 d \cdot (4 d - 1) < n.
  \]
  The last inequality is implied by the inequality where we replace \(4 d - 1\) with \(4 d\), giving the estimate \(d < \sqrt{\frac{n}{8}}\).

title: Corollary

label: lem:tight
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:tight}
  Let \(t(r) = \frac{1}{2 r \cdot (1-r)}\) for \(r \in (0, 1)\) and \(d \geq 2\). Then \(d < t\left(\frac{1}{2 d}\right)\), and moreover, \(d < t\left(\frac{1}{2 d} + \frac{1}{n}\right)\) for \(n \in \NN\) as soon as \(n > 2 d \cdot (d-1) + 2 d \sqrt{d^2 - 2 d}\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Observe that \(t(r)\) is strictly convex with the only minimum at \(\frac{1}{2}\). Consider the equation \(d = t(r)\), that is \(2 d r \cdot (1-r) = 1\), equivalently \(f_d(r) = r^2 - r + \frac{1}{2 d} = 0\) on \(r \in (0,1)\). Then \(f_d\) is strictly convex and has the only minimum at \(r = \frac{1}{2}\). We have \(d < t(r)\) if and only if \(f_d(r) > 0\).

  For the first claim notice that \(f_d\left( \frac{1}{2 d} \right) = \frac{1}{4 d^2} > 0\). For the second claim, consider
  \begin{align*}
    f_d\left( \frac{1}{2 d} + \frac{1}{n} \right)
    = {\left( \frac{1}{2 d} + \frac{1}{n} \right)}^{2} - \frac{1}{n} &> 0 \\
    \frac{1}{4 d^2} + \frac{1}{d n} + \frac{1}{n^2} - \frac{1}{n} &> 0 \\
    n^2 + 4 d n + 4 d^2 - 4 d^2 n &> 0 \\
    n^2 - 4 d \cdot (d-1) \cdot n + 4 d^2 &> 0
  \end{align*}
  Solving this quadratic inequality for \(n\) we get
  \[
    n > 2 d \cdot (d-1) + 2 d \sqrt{(d-1)^2 - 1}
  \]
  and the conclusion follows. Illustrated in \cref{fig:tight}.

title: Remark
body_md: Notice that the condition \(n > 2 d \cdot (4d - 1)\) from \cref{cor:attack} (if we view it as a condition on \(n\) for a fixed \(d\) instead of the other way around) implies the condition \(n > 2 d \cdot (d-1) + 2 d \sqrt{(d-1)^2 - 1}\) in \cref{lem:tight}, thus our reduction in \cref{thm:algo:sampletotal} is not tight for any \(n\) satisfying the necessary condition for security as outlined in \cref{cor:attack}.

label: prop:galois:sqclass
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:galois:sqclass}
  For every \(i \in \ZZ_d\) and \(a \in \FF_q^\star\) for \(q = p^d\) odd prime power, \(a \phi_i(a)\) is a quadratic residue.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: We have \(a \phi_i(a) = a^{p^i + 1}\) with \(p^i + 1\) even.
head: environment

label: prop:galois:sqclassmat
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:galois:sqclassmat}
  Let \(\phi_i \in \operatorname{Gal}(\FF_q/\FF_p)\) and let \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace \in \FF_q^{k \times n}\) generate signed permutation equivalent Galois LCD codes with respect to \(\phi_i\). Then \(\chi_q(\det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\phi_i(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace^\mathtt{T}))) = \chi_q(\det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace\phi_i(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace^\mathtt{T})))\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: There exist \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{O}}\xspace \in \mathcal{O}_n(\ZZ)\) and \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{U}}\xspace \in \mathcal{GL}_k(\FF_q)\) such that \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace = \ensuremath{\mathbf{U}}\xspace\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\ensuremath{\mathbf{O}}\xspace\), hence it holds for Gram matrices that \(\det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace\phi_i(\ensuremath{\mathbf{B}}\xspace^\mathtt{T})) = \det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{U}}\xspace)\phi_i(\det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{U}}\xspace)) \det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\phi_i(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace^\mathtt{T}))\) since \(\phi_i(\ensuremath{\mathbf{O}}\xspace) = \ensuremath{\mathbf{O}}\xspace\). Then use \cref{prop:galois:sqclass} for \(a = \det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{U}}\xspace)\).
head: environment

label: prop:galois:dehull
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:galois:dehull}
  Let \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\) generate an \([n,k]\)-linear code \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) over \(\FF_q\) for \(q=p^d\) odd prime power, and suppose that for some \(i \in \ZZ_d\) we have that \(\operatorname{hull}_{\phi_i}(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace)) = \operatorname{hull}_{\phi_{-i}}(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace))\) and has dimension \(h < k\). The algorithm in \cref{fig:galois:dehull} runs in time \(\bigO{n^\omega}\) and \emph{dehulls} \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\) with respect to \(\phi_i\), that is, finds a matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace \in \FF_q^{(k-h) \times n}\) that generates a Galois LCD code such that \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}} = \operatorname{hull}_{\phi_i}(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}) \oplus \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace)\).
head: environment
name: Galois dehulling

title: Proof
body_md: Using linear algebra, find representatives in \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) for the basis of the quotient \((k-h)\)-dimensional \(\FF_q\)-vector space \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}/\operatorname{hull}_{\phi_i}(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}})\) and store them as \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\). Every \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \in \operatorname{hull}_{\phi_i}(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace))\) is (left and right) \(\phi_i\)-orthogonal to all of \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace)\) and to \(\operatorname{hull}_{\phi_i}(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}})\), hence \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace\) is (left and right) \(\phi_i\)-orthogonal to all of \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\). Thus \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace \in \operatorname{hull}_{\phi_i}(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}})\), and \(\operatorname{hull}_{\phi_i}(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}) \cap \ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace) = \set{\ensuremath{\mathbf{0}}\xspace}\) implies \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}\xspace = \ensuremath{\mathbf{0}}\xspace\).
head: environment

label: def:galois:sqclass
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:galois:sqclass}
  Let \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) be an \([n,k]\)-linear code over \(\FF_q\) for \(q = p^d\) odd prime power, and suppose that for some \(i \in \ZZ_d\) we have that \(\operatorname{hull}_{\phi_i}(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}) = \operatorname{hull}_{\phi_{-i}}(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}})\) and has dimension \(h < k\). The \emph{Galois square class} of \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) with respect to \(\phi_i\) is \(\chi_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}},\phi_i} = \chi_q(\det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\phi_i(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace^\mathtt{T}))) \in \set{\pm 1}\) for any Galois LCD component \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{T}}\xspace\) with respect to \(\phi_i\). When \(h = k\), all codes have square class \(1\).
head: environment
name: Galois square class

label: prop:galois:sqclass:comput
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:galois:sqclass:comput}
  Assume the notation of \cref{def:galois:sqclass}. There is a deterministic algorithm that, given any generator matrix \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\) for \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) and admissible \(i \in \ZZ_d\), computes \(\chi_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}},\phi_i}\) in time \(\bigO{n^\omega + \log^2(q)}\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: If \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) is \(\phi_i\)-self-orthogonal, then output \(\chi_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}},\phi_i} = 1\). Otherwise, dehulling and computing the determinant each take \(\bigO{n^\omega}\) by \cref{prop:galois:dehull}, and applying \(\chi_q\) takes \(\bigO{\log^2(q)}\) by~\cite[1.4.12]{Cohen1993}.

title: Corollary

body_md: Invariance is immediate from \cref{prop:galois:sqclassmat,prop:galois:dehull} and \(\phi(\ensuremath{\mathbf{O}}\xspace) = \ensuremath{\mathbf{O}}\xspace\) for \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{O}}\xspace \in \mathcal{O}_n(\ZZ)\) a signed permutation, efficiency from \cref{prop:galois:sqclass:comput}.

label: prop:galois:sqclass:sym
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:galois:sqclass:sym}
  For every linear code \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) over \(\FF_q\) for \(q = p^d\) odd prime power we have that if \(i \in \ZZ_d\) is such that \(\operatorname{hull}_{\phi_i}(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}) = \operatorname{hull}_{\phi_{-i}}(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}})\), then \(\chi_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}},\phi_i} = \chi_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}},\phi_{-i}}\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Without loss of generality, we may assume \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace)\) is Galois LCD with respect to \(\phi_i\), since a Galois LCD component is well-defined (\cref{prop:galois:dehull}). Then \(\det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\phi_i(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace^\mathtt{T})) = \phi_i(\det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\phi_{-i}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace^\mathtt{T})))\). By \cref{prop:galois:sqclass}, \(a \in \FF_q\) is a quadratic residue if and only if \(\phi_i(a)\) is a quadratic residue, hence \(\chi_q(\det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\phi_i(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace^\mathtt{T}))) = \chi_q(\det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\phi_{-i}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace^\mathtt{T})))\).

label: prop:hermitian:sqclass
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:hermitian:sqclass}
  Assume the notation of \cref{def:galois:sqclass}, and additionally suppose \(d\) is even and fix \(i = \frac{d}{2}\). Then for every linear code \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) we have \(\chi_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}},\phi_i} = 1\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace\) generate \(\ensuremath{\mathfrak{C}}\) and let \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{M}}\xspace = \ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace \phi_i(\ensuremath{\mathbf{A}}\xspace^\mathtt{T})\). Since the form is Hermitian, we have \(\ensuremath{\mathbf{M}}\xspace = \phi_i(\ensuremath{\mathbf{M}}\xspace^\mathtt{T})\). Hence \(\det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{M}}\xspace) = \det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{M}}\xspace^\mathtt{T}) = \det(\phi_i(\ensuremath{\mathbf{M}}\xspace)) = \phi_i(\det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{M}}\xspace))\), so \(\det(\ensuremath{\mathbf{M}}\xspace)\) lies in the subfield \(\FF_{p^\frac{d}{2}}\) fixed by \(\phi_i\). Now observe that every element of \(\FF_{p^\frac{d}{2}}\) is a quadratic residue in \(\FF_{p^d}\); if \(a \in \FF_{p^\frac{d}{2}}\) is embedded into \(\FF_{p^d}\), then \(\chi_{p^d}(a) = a^\frac{p^d-1}{2} = a^{\left(p^\frac{d}{2}-1\right)\cdot\frac{p^\frac{d}{2}+1}{2}} = 1\).
